subject: Route tagging in SDKs (Usage Insights) — API shape + docs commitments (review requested)
related_links: Linear: ENG-8432 (SDKs: add/standardize route tagging helper across SDKs)
body:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Route tagging in SDKs (Usage Insights) — API shape + docs commitments (review requested)

Monica / Elliot / Logan —

As part of Usage Insights (cost drivers by route), we need a consistent way for customers to set a stable “route” identifier per request across SDKs.

I’d like to lock an SDK/API shape this week so Docs can finalize examples and so we don’t end up with 3 different patterns.

Proposal (please sanity check / push back):

1) Canonical concept: route is a user-defined logical endpoint name (e.g., "chat:support_assistant" or "api/v1/answer").
- NOT a URL with dynamic IDs.
- Must comply w/ ADR normalization and cardinality guidance.

2) Wire format: SDKs set a standardized HTTP header on all inference requests:
- Header name: X-Redwood-Route
- Value: customer-supplied route string (pre-normalized client-side where possible; server remains source of truth for normalization)

3) SDK ergonomics (consistent across languages):
- A per-request field called `route` (or `Route`) in the request options.
- Optional client default (client-wide) via `client = Redwood(..., default_route="...")` or equivalent.
- If both are provided, per-request wins.

4) Behavior / edge cases:
- If not set: route becomes "unknown" in console.
- If set but invalid (too long / forbidden chars): SDK should either (a) throw with clear error OR (b) truncate/normalize. I’m leaning (a) fail fast in SDK for developer-controlled issues, but I know this can be contentious.

Docs commitments (Elliot):
- Quickstart snippet updated (Python + TS), plus a small “naming conventions” box.
- Mention “Unknown route” as signal of missing instrumentation.

Monica — can you reply with what’s feasible across TS/Python/Go given existing request option shapes? Also, please tag/loop in the SDK leads if needed; I’m OK with small language-specific differences but want consistent naming.

Logan — any strong constraints from telemetry (e.g., must be request-scoped vs session-scoped)?

If we align by end of day Monday, I’ll send a short decision note + next steps.

Thanks,
Alex

—
Alex Martinez
VP, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference



From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 11:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Route tagging in SDKs (Usage Insights) — API shape + docs commitments (review requested)

+1 on unifying around a header.

Feasibility notes:

TypeScript SDK
- Easiest: add `route?: string` to per-request options (alongside existing `timeout`, `signal`, etc.) and have the transport layer set `X-Redwood-Route`.
- Client default is doable but I’d like to avoid a breaking change in constructor signature; we can add `client.withRoute("...")` or `new Redwood({ defaultRoute: "..." })` depending on current shape.

Python SDK
- We already pass `extra_headers` in some surfaces; but it’s too low-level for docs.
- We can add `route: Optional[str]` to `.responses.create()` / `.chat.completions.create()` equivalents and translate to the header.
- For streaming, this is fine as long as it’s in the initial request.

Go SDK
- We can add a `Route(string)` request option (functional options pattern) and plumb to headers.
- Client-wide default route is a bit awkward in Go; request options are a better fit.

On SDK validation vs server-side:
- I’d vote for client-side *light* validation + normalization (trim, collapse whitespace) but NOT throwing on charset. We’ve seen customers pass things like "api/v1/chat" and "api:v1:chat"; the ADR will standardize anyway.
- Strongly agree we should cap length client-side to protect users from silent drops. Maybe warn/throw only above 128 chars? (Need ADR value.)

Action: I’ll ask TS/Python leads to review by Monday noon and confirm naming and exact field names.

Monica

—
Monica Patel
SDK Coordination Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 12:24 PM PST
Subject: Re: Route tagging in SDKs (Usage Insights) — API shape + docs commitments (review requested)

Telemetry constraints / preferences:

- Must be request-scoped. A “session” default is OK as long as it’s copied onto each request at emit time.
- Header approach is good; gateway and server already have a single place to pull it into request context.
- Please don’t do aggressive client-side normalization beyond trimming. We want server-side normalization to be consistent w/ gateway-derived routes.

Re: invalid values
- We should avoid SDK-side throws except for clearly egregious cases (empty string, > max length). Anything else can be accepted and then normalized/rolled up on ingestion.

Also: we need to reserve (at least) “unknown” and “other” semantics on the backend. Docs should say customers shouldn’t name a route “unknown” intentionally.

Logan

—
Logan Wright
Engineering Manager, Telemetry & Analytics Platform
Redwood Inference



From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 9:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Route tagging in SDKs (Usage Insights) — API shape + docs commitments (review requested)

Docs plan works if we get stable names by Monday end-of-day.

What we’ll ship (docs):
- “Usage Insights: Routes” page (definition, naming conventions, cardinality warnings)
- SDK examples (TS + Python; Go snippet if Monica can provide a minimal one)
- FAQ entry: why you might see “Unknown route” and how to fix

Two specific asks:
1) Confirm the customer-facing field name is `route` (not `route_id`, `routeName`, etc.).
2) Confirm the header name exactly. If we ship “X-Redwood-Route” in docs and then change it later, customers will copy/paste.

No screenshots required for the route tagging section (we’ll do code-first). Console screenshots are separate and can come later.

Elliot

—
Elliot Price
Docs Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 4:28 PM PST
Subject: Re: Route tagging in SDKs (Usage Insights) — API shape + docs commitments (review requested)

Thanks all — aligning on the following (decision for GA docs + SDKs):

Customer-facing SDK parameter name
- `route` (per-request).

Wire format
- HTTP header: `X-Redwood-Route`.

Validation / normalization
- SDKs: trim + reject empty string.
- SDKs: enforce max length (use ADR max; if ADR isn’t explicit, default to 128 chars in SDK and we’ll update once ADR is final). Over-limit should raise a clear client error.
- Everything else: accept and let server-side normalization/rollups handle.

Defaults
- TS/Python: OK to support optional client-wide default route, but not required for GA.
- Go: request option only is fine.

Docs commitments (Elliot)
- You can proceed with `route` + `X-Redwood-Route` in examples.
- Please include a callout: do not use dynamic identifiers (user IDs, UUIDs) in route; “Unknown route” means missing tag.

Monica — can you send review requests to the TS + Python SDK leads today, with a “please approve naming/header by Wed”? If they have objections, let’s keep it in-thread.

Logan — if you can point us at the exact ADR max-length value once finalized, we’ll sync SDK validation.

Alex

—
Alex Martinez
VP, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference
